name: Orient Cement Ltd
title: Orient Cement Ltd - 535754 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Document is an Ambuja Cements Q4 FY26 call transcript (filed under Orient's listing), with Orient only a minor part; cost per tonne peaked at INR4,500, FY27 capex cut to INR6,000–6,500 crore and capacity end-state pushed out, with volume guidance of 80 MT in FY27.

summary.headline: Ambuja Cements FY26: record 73.7 Mt volumes, but Q4 cost ~INR4,500/t; FY27 volume guided ~80 Mt and cost cut of INR250/t targeted.
summary.overview: Ambuja's Q4 FY26 call (consolidating Orient Cement for 11 months and Penna from August 2025) showed record FY26 volumes of 73.7 Mt, up 16% YoY, with normalized FY26 EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (INR887/t, up 12%) and PAT of INR2,647 crore (up 17%). Management said Q4 cost per tonne was about INR4,500, above its earlier INR4,000 exit aspiration, due to acquired-asset underperformance, freight, packing, fuel, branding and repairs. Management called the reset partial: FY28 capacity targets slip toward FY30, capex is cut to INR6,000-6,500 crore for FY27, and the company says cost peaked in Q4. Demand is expected to be soft and industry price hikes are small (about INR10/bag).

financial_highlights.metric: Premium cement share of trade sales

financial_highlights.change: up ~INR1 vs Dec quarter; down vs ~INR255 last year

segments.name: Sanghi Industries (acquired)
segments.commentary: Cement capacity utilization about 57%; management targets 65-70% in FY27. Rail link at Naliya is an add-on, not in base case; seven marine vessels ordered for delivery from next year.

segments.name: Penna Cement (acquired)
segments.commentary: Utilization about 46%; management targets 55-60% in FY27. Breakdowns and deferred maintenance cited; Sanghi and Penna together hold 19 Mt capacity, with a 5-10% utilization uplift targeted.

segments.name: Orient Cement
segments.commentary: Management says Orient is running at full capacity; Orient was consolidated for 11 months in FY26.

segments.name: Ambuja and ACC existing assets
segments.commentary: Management expects 75-80% utilization in FY27; consolidated utilization estimated at 70-75%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated volume guided at ~80 Mt, about 8% growth, versus industry growth of 5-5.5%.
FY27 cost reduction of INR250/t on a full-year average; cost peak of ~INR4,500/t in Q4, Q1 FY27 seen flattish, with savings accelerating over the remaining three quarters.
Minimum cost reduction of INR250/t in FY27 and another INR250/t in FY28 (INR500 cumulative); management says the earlier INR3,650/t target is not abandoned.

Capacity to reach ~119 Mt by end FY27 after ~10 Mt of additions (commissioning Aug-Sep 2026 window); FY28 target capacity slips toward FY30; Maratha adds 4 Mt clinker; Mundra (2 Mt clinker) and Assam (2 Mt clinker) follow in about 24-28 months.
FY27 capex estimated at INR6,000-6,500 crore; project IRR hurdle of 18% stated.
Management did not give EBITDA/t guidance; said it is too early to estimate given volatility.
capex_capacity: Capacity 109 Mt at FY26 end after 10.7 Mt grinding and 7 Mt clinker added (Marwar, Farakka, Sankrail, Sindri, Krishnapatnam, Jodhpur, Bhatapara).
Clinker capacity 69 Mt now, rising to 73 Mt with Maratha (4 Mt).
About INR4,000 crore of capex already under execution (capacity, WHRS, fly ash transport); balance is debottlenecking and maintenance.

Recalibrating growth capex: shutting some grinding units in North UP, Bihar, South Gujarat and Maharashtra to move them closer to markets; a Bihar grinding unit planned; Dahej Line 2 as clinker-plus-cement example.
Management paused new projects until current ones are completed; engineering to be finalized over next 6 months.
demand_pricing: Industry price rise in March quarter was about INR10/bag, INR15-20 only in selected pockets; management says industry cannot pass on costs under relentless pricing pressure.
April-May demand described as subdued and soft; management would be happy if industry recovers half of a price hike.
Q4 FY26 volume growth was muted (Orient-adjusted flat YoY per an analyst); packing bag shortages linked to West Asia conflict cost volume in March.
Premium cement gap versus base product INR50-55/bag for super premium and INR20-25/bag for premium; price gap with the number-one player is INR5-10 in some districts.
Management expects FY27 demand to be soft due to inflation and weak monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 cost about INR4,500/t when management earlier pointed to an INR4,000 exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,000 was an aspiration for the March exit; March averaged ~INR4,100 normalized, with INR250 escalation from West Asia. Causes cited: branding, repairs at acquired plants, freight, packing, fuel and heat consumption, and lower government incentives.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost reduction is assumed for FY27 after Q4 inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,500 is the peak; a INR250/t reduction gives ~INR4,250/t for FY27 on a full-year average, with Q1 FY27 flat at ~INR4,500.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR3,650/t cost target be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said the target is not abandoned; INR500/t cumulative over two years is the committed minimum, with further runway to the earlier target.

qa_highlights.question: Why the reset in capacity and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said performance fell short of commitments, citing cost, wrong contractor choice, projects started without full engineering, and breakdowns at Penna and Sanghi; ~80% of the five KPIs relate to cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a target IRR for capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani stated a project IRR of 18%, all equity-funded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cause of high working capital and negative ACC operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinod Bahety said ACC has MSA receivables from Ambuja that will be settled via an ICD after shareholder approval; Ambuja's core working capital fell to 20 days from 30 days.

risks_watch: Cost trajectory: whether Q1 FY27 holds near INR4,500/t and the INR250/t FY27 reduction is delivered.
Acquired-asset utilization at Sanghi (57%) and Penna (46%) and reliability of Penna and Sanghi plants.
Pricing power in a soft demand environment; April-May trend described as subdued.
Capex execution delays (Maratha, Chhattisgarh) and capex recalibration; 10 Mt commissioning between now and September.
Non-core working capital, MSA receivables from ACC, and negative ACC operating cash flow, to be resolved via ICD.
Reduced government incentives after GST rate cuts and changed accrual policy.
summary.management_tone: Candid and self-critical on execution, with management admitting missed targets and a partial reset in timelines. Confident on controllable cost levers, but evasive on EBITDA/t guidance and on pricing outlook, which they called soft.
key_quotes: Therefore, I strongly believe INR150 to INR200 savings will come from these components.
So we are not shying away from our target.
So we'll be honest with you. Yes, partially, there is a reset.
Yes, we are moving away from the time line.
But I think any guidance on EBITDA will be difficult at this stage.

adds.what: ~10 Mt grinding capacity additions (commissioning Aug-Sep 2026 window), taking total to ~119 Mt by end FY27

growth.why: Management guides FY27 consolidated volume of ~80 Mt (~8% growth) backed by ~10 Mt of grinding additions due Aug-Sep 2026 and utilisation uplift at acquired Sanghi (57%) and Penna (46%), though demand is expected soft and capacity end-state has slipped toward FY30.
